evidence:
Scope is the workbook's syntax and reference-entry check, not a claim that the full judge suite has run. Inspected the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A52:D52 gives check 51 and says "task.toml, scoring.toml, every judge.toml, the shell scripts (bash -n, no CRLF), and the reference/app entry"; Internal Quality Checks!A52:D52 repeats "both TOML families" and has no additional annotation or cell comment. Read frozen Harbor SKILL.md, quality-checks.md section 51, deterministic-checks.md parser/verifier/solve recipes, staged-task-contract.md entry/shell structure, and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md runtime-evidence distinctions.

Observed read-only parser checks on the frozen task: Python 3.12 tomllib.loads succeeds on all 7 TOMLs (task.toml, tests/scoring.toml, both gates' judge.toml and all three scored dimensions' judge.toml). json.loads succeeds on all 4 JSON files (seed_data.json, package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json). ast.parse succeeds on both tests/tools Python files. Both shipped .sh files were enumerated: solution/solve.sh has 26 LF characters and zero CR/CRLF; tests/test.sh has 227 LF characters and zero CR/CRLF. Both start with '#!/bin/bash' at line 1. C:/Users/00518507/AppData/Local/Programs/Git/bin/bash.exe --noprofile --norc -n, fed each exact file as stdin, returns 0 and empty stderr for both. The generated restart shell heredoc at tests/test.sh:127 also passes bash -n; all three embedded Python heredocs beginning at lines 43, 131 and 195 compile successfully. The initial system32 WSL bash attempt returned Bash/Service/CreateInstance/E_ACCESSDENIED; the installed Git Bash successfully completed the same checks, so this is not a task parser error or unresolved measurement.

Node --check succeeds for server.js as CommonJS, vite.config.mjs as an ES module, src/vendor.js as an ES module, and public/assets/index-0TNzM6xa.js as an ES module. Inline scripts in both static/runner.html and public/runner.html, counter.html, and all three JavaScript starters also parse. The parser mode is grounded in solution/app/package.json:5 ('"type": "commonjs"') and solution/app/public/index.html:1 ('<script type="module" ... src="/assets/index-0TNzM6xa.js">'). Both production JS and CSS references in public/index.html:1-2 exist. server.js:101 serves the public folder; server.js:113 listens on the requested port and line 115 initializes SQLite. The intentionally throwing starter is documented: starters/broken.js:1 says 'Kept on purpose: this one throws'; its runtime TypeError is playground input, not an entry-point parse defect.

Runtime corroboration is independent of syntax: verified RESULTS.json SHA256 ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09 against raw-evidence-index.json, and all 22 actual_app_files hashes match the frozen solution/app bytes. Verified hashes of launch_workflow.py, run_workflow.cjs, workflow_core.cjs, current_flow.cjs and workspace_flow.cjs against that raw result. launch_workflow.py:37-38 launches the app as uid/gid 65534 using NODE_PATH, PORT and DB_PATH; lines 52-57 require a successful health response. workspace_flow.cjs:45-50 opens the actual UI, waits for completion, and reads source/preview/console; lines 65-70 execute an authored edit. In RESULTS.json /facts/S01.startup_ready/evidence/value, filename is hello.js, preview contains '12 squared is 144', console contains the log and 12, and status is 'Complete ... 5.9 ms'; /facts/S01.usable_examples/evidence/value/authored/body is 'example-authored-marker'. /pre/browser_errors and /pre/own_browser_errors are empty. This verifies execution of the exact shipped app and avoids inferring launch success solely from parsing. These are direct scripted browser observations; no full configured judge run, Oracle score, target-model result, or LLM judge workload is claimed. Those broader measurements remain unmeasured outside this check's well-formed-file scope.
counterexample: Actually tested parser controls in memory: valid 'export const x = 1;' passes Node --input-type=module --check (exit 0), but the identical valid browser module fails forced CommonJS parsing (exit 1, SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'). Using the browser module mode prevents this false failure for the shipped module bundle. Broken 'const app = ;' is rejected (exit 1, SyntaxError: Unexpected token ';'). Syntactically valid require('missing-runtime-module') passes --check (exit 0), demonstrating that a broken runtime could falsely pass syntax-only review. The hash-bound real server launch plus browser-authored execution supplies the additional runtime corroboration for this candidate; no task files were mutated to construct these controls.
